title: Coin Change
description:
You have coin denominations in the array coins and want to make exactly amount units. You may use each denomination any number of times. Return the fewest coins needed, or -1 when the amount cannot be formed. A coin contributes its face value; the arrangement of coins does not affect the minimum. Denominations may arrive in any order, and there is no promise that choosing the biggest coin first will succeed.

Think of every smaller total as a subproblem: an optimal way to form total x can finish with some denomination c, following an optimal way to form x-c. Begin with a cost of zero for total zero and mark unreachable totals distinctly. Comparing all permitted last coins gives the answer without assuming a greedy currency system.

An empty set of denominations can form only zero. The target zero always takes zero coins, even if the denominations list is empty. Duplicate denominations do not change the answer, and a denomination bigger than the target cannot help. Do not return a coin combination: only the numerical minimum is graded. In particular, with denominations 1, 3, and 4, six is best made by two threes rather than 4+1+1.

Example 1:

Input: coins = [1,3,4], amount = 6
Output: 2

Example 2:

Input: coins = [2], amount = 3
Output: -1

Example 3:

Input: coins = [], amount = 0
Output: 0

Constraints:

  • 0 <= coins.length <= 30
  • 1 <= coins[i] <= 10,000
  • 0 <= amount <= 10,000
  • Coins can be reused without limit.
